Introduction

Easy2edit is a simple, modular management system (CMS) for building and running portals, websites, webshops and communities. It is designed so that you can start quickly with a ready-made setup, and then grow the site by switching modules and plugins on or off, without needing to touch any code.

Behind the scenes, Easy2edit runs on a Django (REST) backend and a Next.js frontend. You do not need to know anything about these technologies to use the system. What matters for you as an administrator or website owner is that the site is built from blocks, and that features of the site can be turned on or off as modules and plugins.

## How a site is built

Rather than writing pages from scratch, you build a website from blocks. These blocks are combined into pages, and pages are combined into a complete site. On top of that, you decide which parts of the system are active by switching modules and plugins on or off. This makes it possible to keep a site simple and light, or to expand it with more functionality as your needs grow.

## Who uses Easy2edit

There are three kinds of people who work with an Easy2edit site:

- Users: visitors who have created an account on the site. They can log in, manage their own profile and use the features that are available to them.
- Admins: people who manage parts of the site. What an admin is allowed to do depends on the roles assigned to them. One admin might only manage pages, while another might also manage plugins or users, depending on their role.
- Superadmins: the owner or reseller of the site. A superadmin can do everything, including changing system settings, switching modules and plugins on or off, managing prices and managing the licence.

This structure means that you can safely delegate day to day management tasks to admins, while keeping full control over the system as a superadmin.

## The dashboard

After logging in, you work from the dashboard. The dashboard is organised into three areas:

- Dashboard: this is your own personal area, where you manage your own profile, see your notifications and view your own AI credit.
- Admin: this is the management area, where admins manage the parts of the site they are responsible for.
- Super admin: this is the system area, reserved for superadmins, where system-wide settings are configured.

Which of these areas you see, and what you can do inside them, depends on whether you are a user, an admin or a superadmin.

## Modules and plugins

Easy2edit is modular, which means that functionality is organised into modules and plugins that can be switched on or off as needed.

Modules are parts of the system that can be enabled or disabled. You manage them under Super admin > Modules.

Plugins are signed extension packages. They bring their own pages and their own modules with them, extending what the site can do. You manage plugins under Admin > Plugins.

Because modules and plugins can be switched on or off, you only need to activate the parts of the system that your site actually needs, keeping things clear and manageable.

## Standard installations

To help you get started quickly, Easy2edit offers standard installations. A standard installation sets up the modules, plugins and theme for a particular type of website with a single click. Available types include:

- Standard website
- Web shop
- Company website
- Business network
- Intranet
- Dating platform
- Sports club
- Foundation
- Marketplace
- Game hall

Each standard installation is shown as a small tile, visible in the admin area. The tile has a settings pop-up, which is offered the first time you install it. From this pop-up you can configure things such as AI credit settings, which modules are included, and whether demo data is added.

## The header

At the top of the screen, the header gives you quick access to a few general controls:

- The language switcher, to change the display language.
- The edit-mode switch (shown as a pencil icon), to turn editing of the site on or off.
- Light and dark mode, to switch the appearance of the interface.
- The user menu, where you can access your account options.

These header controls are available wherever you are in the system, so you can always adjust your language, switch between viewing and editing the site, change the display mode, or access your user menu.
Getting started

## First login

The first time you log in to Easy2edit, use the superadmin account. As soon as you log in, a welcome pop-up appears that explains the AI credit included with your installation. From this pop-up you can put the AI credit settings in place straight away (see the AI chapter for the full details on tokens, costs and margins).

Once you have handled the welcome pop-up, you are ready to configure the basics of your website.

## Setting up the basics

Easy2edit is built to get you online quickly. Work through the following steps in order:

1. Go to Admin > System and fill in the basics: your site name, company data, contact data and addresses. This information is used throughout the website and in system communication.

2. Pick a starting point for your site structure. You can choose a standard installation from the Super admin overview or from Admin > Standard installations. This gives you a ready-made set of pages, menus and settings to build on.

3. Go to Admin > Theme and Admin > Logos & images to choose a theme and upload your logos. This determines the look and feel of your website, including colors, fonts and branding.

4. Go to Admin > Languages to choose which languages your website should support. If you only need one language, you can leave multilingual support switched off.

5. Go to Admin > Users and Roles to create the user accounts and roles your team needs, and to assign the right permissions to each role.

After these five steps, your website has a name, a look, a language setup and the right people with access. From here you can start editing content and switching on the modules you need.

## Getting to know the modules

Easy2edit is built from modules: separate building blocks that you can switch on or off depending on what your website needs. A full overview, with the ability to turn each module on or off, is available to superadmins at Admin > Modulebeheer.

The modules cover a wide range of areas, for example:

- Content and pages: Pages and menu, Edit mode, Media library, Site import, System objects, Logos & images, Theme, Languages, SEO, FAQ, Privacy and cookie pages.

- Commerce: Subscriptions, Donations, Orders, Payments.

- Community and communication: Profiles & blocking, Discover, Messages, Chat, Direct connect, Notifications.

- Compliance and protection: Country control, Age gate, Gambling popup, Cookies, Word filter, Registration, Two-factor authentication.

- System and technical: API keys, Communication, Plugins, Sandbox, System basics, Storage structure, Statistics, Backup, Roles, Users, Dashboard & profile, Basic security, AI, Module management.

Some modules, such as Orders and Payments, are plugins that must first be switched on at Admin > Plugins; the related module page only lets you set who is allowed to use them. Pages, menu and edit mode

This chapter explains how pages and the menu work in Easy2edit, and how to build and edit page content using edit mode.

## Pages and menu overview

Go to Admin > Pages to manage everything related to your site structure. This is where you find:

- System pages, such as Home and products, which are part of the core setup of your site.
- Own pages, which are simple text pages available at an address such as /p/<key>.
- Links and menu items, which let you point the menu to internal pages or external addresses without creating a full page.

## Page settings

Each page has its own set of settings that control how it looks, who can see it and where it appears.

- Names per language. You can set a different name for each language, and use AI translation to automatically translate the name into all other active languages.
- Address per language. Each language can have its own address for the page.
- Visibility. Choose who may see the page: everybody, only logged-in users, only guests, or specific users or groups.
- Menu display. Decide whether the page should show in the header menu.
- New tab. Choose whether the page should open in a new browser tab when clicked.
- Devices. Control whether the page is shown on desktop, tablet and/or mobile.
- Theme, header and footer. A page can use its own theme, header or footer instead of the site-wide default.
- SEO per language. Set SEO details separately for each language.
- Background. Add a background image or video to the page.

## Switching on edit mode

To start editing the content of a page, click the pencil icon in the header. This switches the page into edit mode, where you can add, change and arrange content directly on the page.

## Rows, cells and items

Pages in Easy2edit are built from rows, which act as horizontal blocks of content.

- Each row can be divided into cells, from 1 up to 4 columns.
- Each cell can contain one or more items, which are the actual pieces of content.

Available items include:

- Heading
- Text (rich text)
- Image
- Button
- Spacer
- Line
- System objects
- Ready-made parts: contact data, social media, map, video, quote, figures, logo, opening hours
- HTML / CSS code

## Row settings

Click the gear icon in the corner of a row to open its settings. From here you can adjust:

- Background colour, image or video
- Overlay
- Padding
- Width: column, wide or full screen
- Hero height
- Text colour
- Rounded corners
- Space above the row

## Cell settings

Each cell within a row also has its own settings, including:

- Width
- Alignment
- Card style: background, border, radius and shadow

## Text and button settings

Text items can be styled individually with:

- Style, size, colour and font
- Padding
- Background, shown as a label or pill

Button items can be configured with:

- Label per language
- Link
- Style: primary, outline or ghost
- Colours
- Size
- Icon

## The HTML / CSS code part

For advanced or custom content, you can add the HTML / CSS code item. This opens a large pop-up with three tabs:

- Visual. Click directly in the text area and type; this works as what you see is what you get. A toolbar offers bold, italic, underline, list, link and clear formatting, plus a light or dark background switch.
- HTML. Edit the underlying HTML code directly.
- CSS. Edit the styling for this piece of content.

The code you enter runs inside a sandboxed frame, which means it has no rights on the rest of the site. This keeps your website safe even when custom code is used.

## System objects

System objects let you place dynamic, module-based content into a page. These must first be enabled in Admin > System objects. Available system objects include:

- Donation buttons
- Subscriptions
- Media views
- Plugin parts
- AI dashboard blocks (visible to superadmins only)

To add one, go into edit mode on a page and choose + Add > System objects, then select the object you want to place.

## Editing pages imported from HTML

If a page was taken over 1 to 1 from an HTML file during site import, it behaves slightly differently in edit mode. Every text and button on such a page shows its own pencil icon.

1. Click the pencil next to the text or button you want to change.
2. An editor opens showing the content as it appears on the page, with formatting options for bold, italic, underline and link, and for buttons, the link address.
3. Make your changes in the editor.
4. Click Save to write the changes back into the page.

This approach lets you safely update imported HTML pages without needing to rebuild them with rows and cells.
Importing a website (Site import)

Easy2edit can import an existing website for you. Point it at one or more HTML files, a web address, a folder, or a ZIP file, and the built-in AI will study the content and prepare a proposal for your approval. Nothing is created on your site until you say so.

You manage this feature from Admin > Imported. Before you have imported anything, the button is labelled Site import. Once an import has taken place, the same button is called Imported.

## Starting an import

1. Go to Admin > Imported and choose Site import.
2. Drop one or more HTML files, or provide an address, a folder, or a ZIP file.
3. The AI reads the files and prepares a proposal. This includes:
   - A theme: colours, fonts, corner roundings, and content width.
   - The pages found in the source.
   - The content of those pages.
   - Icons and images, which are placed in the media library and tagged import.
   - Any modules that seem necessary, for example the FAQ module when the source contains lists of questions and answers.
4. Review the proposal. Nothing is built or installed until you approve it.

## Approving the proposal

Once you approve, the proposed theme is installed and put into use straight away. After that, you move on to the Apply step, where a pop-up or panel appears with several tabs: Pages, Links, Buttons, Header, Footer, and Theme.

## Pages tab

This tab shows two columns: pages from the imported file on the left, and the pages of your own website on the right. Drag a file from the left to a page on the right to link them, for example linking the imported home page to your existing Home page. If you leave a file unlinked, it becomes a new page of its own.

For each linked or new page, choose a view:

- Exact: the page looks exactly like the original HTML file. You can still edit texts and buttons afterwards using the pencil in edit mode.
- Editable: the AI rebuilds the page using the blocks of the page builder. Cards, label pills, coloured bands, rows, and the hero section are recreated as blocks. Anything the blocks cannot reproduce, such as a progress bar, check lists, or preview cards, is placed in an HTML / CSS code block instead.

You can also give the AI an optional instruction for how to handle the page, for example "make the headings bigger."

For pages that already have content, decide what should happen to it:

- Clear the existing content first.
- Replace only the blocks created by this import, leaving other content untouched.
- Add the imported content below what is already there.

You can also choose whether the pages should be translated into your site's other languages.

## Links and Buttons tabs

In these tabs you connect the links and buttons found in the imported file to pages or sections of your own website, again using drag and drop.

## Header and Footer tabs

The Header tab lets you switch your site's header to the header from the imported file, which typically brings a larger menu including the links and buttons found there. The Footer tab lets you show the footer from the import underneath your pages.

## Theme tab

Here you fine-tune the theme that was installed: colours, the default light or dark mode, content width, and corner roundings.

## Running the import

Once everything is set in the Apply panel, start the process. Progress is shown in a pop-up with a percentage. When it finishes, a Go to page button appears so you can view the result straight away.

The original HTML file is always kept, so you can run Apply again later with a new instruction if you want to adjust the result.

## Managing imports afterwards

Each import has a status, either Pending or Active, visible in Admin > Imported. The list of pages belonging to an import shows, per page: its name, whether it appears in the menu, whether it is visible, and which view (Exact or Editable) is used.

For an individual imported page, go to Pages > page settings. There you will find an Import tab where you can give the AI a specific instruction and use a button to rebuild just that one page from the original file, without affecting the rest of the import.

## Removing an import

If you remove an import, Easy2edit restores the theme and content that was in place before the import, and removes everything the import created. In some cases, it will advise re-installing via the superadmin instead.

Note that the standard home page, with its default logo, title, text, and photos, is always empty by default. An import always overwrites it, so the default content never shows behind an imported home page.
Media, theme, languages and branding

This chapter covers the parts of Easy2edit that control how your website looks and feels, and how your media and content are made available to visitors in different languages.

## Media library

The media library is where you manage all images and videos used throughout your website, whether they are stored locally or on an external storage service such as S3.

Every image or video you upload can be given tags, which makes it much easier to find the right file later, especially once your library grows. Once a picture is in the library, it becomes available for selection in every pop-up throughout Easy2edit, so you only need to upload a file once and can reuse it wherever you need it.

Practical tips for working with the media library:

- Upload images and videos in advance, before you start building a page, so you can simply pick them from the library while editing.
- Use clear, consistent tags (for example by subject, page, or campaign) so files stay easy to find.
- Reuse existing media instead of uploading duplicates, to keep your library tidy and save storage space.

## Logos and images (branding)

The branding settings let you control the key visual elements that represent your organisation across the website. This includes:

- The logo, with separate versions for light and dark mode
- The favicon, shown in browser tabs
- The app icon, used when the site is saved to a home screen
- The photos displayed on the homepage

Keeping these elements up to date ensures your website looks professional and consistent, and that your brand is recognisable in browser tabs, bookmarks, and on mobile home screens.

## Theme (Admin > Theme)

The theme settings determine the overall look and feel of your website. Here you can adjust:

- Colours for both light mode and dark mode
- Fonts used across the site
- Roundings (how sharp or soft corners and edges appear)
- Content width
- Header layout, including an editorial layout with a side menu
- Pop-up style

If the theme feature is switched off, the website uses the standard style instead of your custom settings.

Theme packs let you change the entire look of your website in one click. Rather than adjusting colours, fonts, and layout settings one by one, you can select a theme pack that applies a complete, coordinated style instantly. This is useful if you want to try out a different look quickly or want to keep a consistent style across multiple projects.

Exporting and importing themes gives you additional flexibility:

- Export a theme to save your current style settings or to reuse them on another website.
- Import a theme to apply a previously saved style, which is helpful when managing several websites that should share the same look, or when restoring a style you created earlier.

Steps to apply a theme pack:

1. Go to Admin > Theme.
2. Browse the available theme packs.
3. Select the theme pack you want to use.
4. Review the result on your website, since colours, fonts and layout will update immediately.

## Languages

The languages feature controls whether your website is available in multiple languages or only in a single, default language. If languages are switched off, visitors only see the website in the standard language.

When languages are switched on, you can:

- Choose which languages your website offers to visitors
- Set the default language that visitors see first
- Translate texts using the built-in AI translation feature

This makes it possible to reach a wider audience without manually rewriting every page in each language. The AI translation feature can give you a solid starting point, which you can then review and refine where needed.

It is worth noting that the system itself, meaning menus, labels and other interface texts, is already available in 44 languages. This means administrators and editors can often work in their own language, regardless of which languages are offered to website visitors.

## Putting it together

Media, branding, theme and language settings work together to shape the overall experience of your website:

- Use the media library to organise and reuse your visual content efficiently.
- Set up logos and images once, and update them whenever your branding changes.
- Use the theme settings, or a theme pack, to quickly establish a consistent visual style, and export or import themes when working across multiple sites.
- Decide whether your website needs multiple languages, and if so, configure them and use AI translation to speed up the process.

Taking time to set these up carefully early on will save effort later, since changes here affect the entire website rather than individual pages.
Users, roles and security

This chapter explains how to manage who can access your website and your admin area, and how to protect both your visitors and your content with the built-in security tools.

## Users

Every person who needs access to the admin area or who has a public profile on the website is set up as a user. In Admin > Users you can:

- Create new accounts
- Add a profile photo
- Block an account temporarily
- Delete an account permanently

A blocked account cannot log in, but its data and content remain in the system until you decide to delete it. Each user can also have a public profile, which is useful if visitors should be able to see who wrote an article or who moderates a section of the site.

## User groups

If several users need the same access, you can organise them into user groups. A group combines a set of roles and module access, so you only need to configure permissions once and then add or remove users from the group as needed. This is the easiest way to manage access for teams, such as editors, moderators or support staff.

## Roles

Roles (Admin > Rollen) define exactly what a user or group is allowed to do. A role is a set of rights, for example:

- Content manager
- Moderator
- View AI use of users

Each right unlocks a specific part of the admin area. You can assign one or more roles to a user or to a user group.

If the Rollen module is switched off, only superadmins have any rights at all. Superadmins always have full access to every part of the system, regardless of the roles configured.

Steps to assign a role:

1. Go to Admin > Rollen.
2. Open or create the role you want to use.
3. Add the rights that belong to this role.
4. Assign the role to the relevant user or user group.

## Module access per user or group

Besides roles, access to individual modules can also be granted directly to a specific user or group. This is managed in Super admin > Modules, using the person icon next to a module. This gives you fine control in cases where someone needs access to one particular module without needing a full role.

## Dashboard and your own profile

Once logged in, every user lands on their dashboard. From there, users can manage their own profile, including their photo and personal details. The dashboard is also the starting point for reaching the parts of the admin area that the user has rights for.

## General security

The Algemene beveiliging module covers the core security settings for the admin area:

- Login lock: blocks further login attempts after repeated failures, to protect against brute-force attacks
- Session duration: controls how long a user stays logged in before needing to log in again
- Password rules: enforce minimum requirements for passwords created by your users
- Security headers: technical HTTP headers that help protect the website against common attacks

Two-step verification is also available as an extra layer of login security, requiring a second confirmation step in addition to the password.

It is recommended to review these settings when setting up a new site, and to keep password rules and session duration suited to how sensitive the content of your site is.

## Country control

The Landcontrole module lets you block or allow access to your website per country, based on the visitor's IP address. This is useful if your content or products are only relevant, or only legally allowed, in certain countries.

## Age and gambling checks

Some websites are required to confirm the age of their visitors or to show responsible-use warnings:

- Leeftijdscontrole shows an 18+ popup to visitors before they can view the site
- Gokken-popup shows a combined age and warning popup specifically intended for gambling-related content

Enable the module that matches your legal requirements; both can be configured without needing developer support.

## Cookies

The Cookies module provides the cookiebanner that visitors see, lets them set their cookie preferences, and links to your cookie policy popup. This helps you meet legal requirements around informing visitors about cookie use and obtaining their consent where needed.

## Word filter

The Woordfilter module automatically checks for forbidden words in texts, names and captions entered on your website. This is useful for keeping user-generated content, such as comments, profile names or captions, free of unwanted language without needing to review every entry manually.
Shop, orders, payments, subscriptions and donations

Easy2edit lets you sell products, collect donations and run subscriptions using a set of plugins that work together. This chapter explains how the pieces fit together and how to set each one up.

## How the plugins work together

Selling anything on your site, whether it is a physical product, a subscription or a donation, involves several plugins that depend on each other:

- Webshop handles products, product groups, variants and shipping, and needs the Orders and Betalen (Payment) plugins to function.
- Orders manages bestellingen (orders) for the whole site: webshop orders, subscription orders and donations. It can also work on its own if you only accept payment by invoice. Orders needs the Betalen and Webshop plugins.
- Financieel (Finance) brings together payment methods, payment terms, the links to Stripe and Mollie, VAT rates, shipping options and the layout of invoices, quotes, packing slips and return slips. Orders, Webshop and Abonnementen (Subscriptions) all need this plugin.
- Abonnementen (Subscriptions) manages subscription plans and donation campaigns. It needs the Orders plugin.

Because of these dependencies, activate the plugins in this order: Betalen, Orders, Financieel, and then Webshop and/or Abonnementen depending on what you want to offer.

## Setting up the webshop

The Webshop plugin lets you build an online store with:

- Products and product groups to organise your catalogue.
- Variants such as colour or size, each with its own price.
- Staffelprijzen (tiered pricing), so the price can change depending on the quantity ordered.
- Shipping methods and discount codes.
- Several layouts, including a standard layout and an editorial layout with a filter side panel and a large product photo, plus a 'shop the look' option, with their own styles and presets.

The plugin comes with demo content, including ready-made pages for products, the shopping cart and checkout, so you can see a working shop immediately after activation and adjust it to your needs.

To set up a product:

1. Go to Admin > Webshop and create a product group if you want to organise products into categories.
2. Add a new product and fill in its details, price and description.
3. Add any variants, such as colour or size, and set a price for each if needed.
4. If relevant, set up staffelprijzen for quantity discounts.
5. Choose or confirm the shipping method for the product.

## Managing orders

The Orders plugin is the central place for everything related to orders across the whole site, whether they come from the webshop, a subscription or a donation. From Admin > Orders you can:

- View and manage all bestellingen in one overview.
- Track and update the order status.
- Configure btw-instellingen (VAT settings) for orders.
- Edit the confirmation email that customers receive after placing an order.

Orders also produces the documents customers and your administration need, such as the packing slip, invoice, return slip and credit invoice.

If you do not want to use the webshop or online payments at all, Orders can still work on its own, allowing customers to pay per factuur (by invoice).

## Payments and finance settings

The Financieel plugin is where you manage everything related to money:

- Payment methods and payment terms.
- The koppelingen (connections) to Stripe and Mollie for processing online payments.
- Btw-tarieven: by default a standard high and a low VAT rate, which you link to individual products.
- Shipping options.
- The layout of invoices, quotes, packing slips and return slips, along with your company data.

Payments themselves are carried out through Stripe or Mollie. Both providers offer a sandbox mode, which lets you simulate payments safely while testing your shop or subscription setup, without processing real transactions.

To connect a payment provider:

1. Go to Admin > Financieel.
2. Enter your Stripe or Mollie account details to create the koppeling.
3. Use the sandbox option while testing, and switch to live mode once you are ready to accept real payments.
4. Review and set your btw-tarieven and link them to the relevant products.
5. Check the layout of your invoices, quotes and other documents, and add your company details.

## Subscriptions and donations

The Abonnementen plugin lets you offer paid access to parts of your site, such as pages, content, chat, video, likes or services. Plans can be:

- Eenmalig (one-off), billed once.
- Herhaald (recurring), with a new order generated automatically for each period.

Abonnementen also supports donatie-acties (donation campaigns), where visitors choose an amount themselves using a slider, moving between a minimum and a maximum amount that you set.

In addition, acties (promotions) within this plugin let you decide which parts of your site are free and which require payment, giving you flexibility to offer a mix of free and paid content.

To set up a subscription plan:

1. Go to Admin > Abonnementen.
2. Create a new plan and decide whether it is eenmalig or herhaald.
3. Link the plan to the pages, content or services it should unlock.
4. Set the price, and for recurring plans, the billing period.

To set up a donation campaign:

1. Create a new donatie-actie in Admin > Abonnementen.
2. Set the minimum and maximum amount for the slider.
3. Publish the campaign on the relevant page so visitors can contribute.
Community, marketplace, agenda, documents and games

Easy2edit offers a set of plugins that turn your site into a social platform. Together they let members build a profile, find and contact each other, trade items, manage appointments, share documents and play games. This chapter describes each of these building blocks and how they fit together.

## Community overview

The Community plugin brings together everything you need for a community or dating site. Members get their own profile pages with photos, can search for other members, and can block users they do not want to interact with. They can search and match with others: liking profiles, keeping favorites and seeing who visited their page. Members can also exchange messages, use chat, and set up a direct connection (WebRTC) using a code, a link or a QR code.

Community profiles use profile themes, profile fields and "available for" options, so you can tailor the experience to your audience. When parts of the community require a subscription or a donation, the Community plugin works together with the Subscriptions plugin.

## Profile themes

Profile themes let you package a set of profile fields and settings for a specific type of community. Easy2edit comes with ready-made themes:

- Sporters
- Dating
- Business
- Webshop

You can install or remove these themes, or create your own with custom fields, visibility settings and search filters. As superadmin, you decide which themes administrators and users are allowed to choose. Themes can be exported and imported as JSON files, which makes it easy to reuse a theme on another site or share it with others.

## Marketplace

The marketplace lets members offer products, services or other items for sale. Each listing can have its own theme and images. Sellers can choose how an item is offered:

- A fixed price
- Bidding, starting from a minimum price
- A booking, for example an appointment or registration for an event

Bids are visible to all members, so the marketplace works in an open, transparent way, similar to an auction.

## Agenda

The agenda gives users and groups a way to manage appointments and events. It supports several types of entries:

- Personal appointments
- Appointments with other members, including invitations, confirmations or proposing an alternative time
- Group appointments
- Events created by administrators, which can be placed on pages as a system object

The agenda includes reminders and notifications, and members can see upcoming items through a tile on the dashboard.

## Document management

Document management allows you to upload documents into a folder structure, complete with tags, version history and access rights per user or per group. Files can be stored on the server or on S3, and can be encrypted for extra security. Blocks are available so you can display documents directly on pages.

To set up document access for a specific audience:

1. Create the folder structure that matches how your organization works.
2. Upload documents and add tags to make them easy to find.
3. Set rights per user or per group, so only the right people can view or edit each document.
4. Place a document block on a page if you want visitors to see selected documents there.

## Games

The games hall gives your members a place to play. Each game is its own package, delivered as a folder or a zip file containing a game.json file, placed in the games folder of the games plugin. Every game has its own configuration for management and its own settings per member.

Games run in an isolated, protected environment and automatically save scores and progress. Ranked lists let members compare their results, and a sample game is included so you can see how a game package is structured before adding your own.

## Age, country and gambling checks

Some community and marketplace features are only appropriate for certain audiences, so Easy2edit includes age verification (18+), country checks and a gambling popup (24+). These checks should only be enabled for the target groups where they are required or desired.

The settings for these checks are found under Admin > Beveiliging (Security). Keep in mind that the popups and the country check only work when the relevant plugin is switched on.

## The building blocks behind Community

The Community plugin is built from several smaller plugins, which you can also find and manage individually:

- Profiles: the personal profile page with multiple photos, visibility per language and group, the member search and the option to block other users.
- Discover: searching for and meeting other users, similar to a dating site, with filters, recommendations, likes, matches, favorites and visitors.
- Messages: the messaging system between users, with its own inbox.
- Chat: chat in a popup or full screen, either through the portal or directly between members using WebRTC, including photos, videos and video chat.
- Direct connect: a direct WebRTC connection between two people using a code, a link or a QR code, available even without an account. This includes chat, photos, videos and video chat, accessible through the /directconnect and /direct pages.

Because these are separate plugins underneath the Community umbrella, you can enable only the parts you need, or use them independently if you do not want a full community setup.
SEO, FAQ and statistics

## SEO

Easy2edit helps your website get found and understood, not only by traditional search engines but also by bots and AI agents. The SEO tools take care of the technical and content-related elements that search engines and AI systems use to index and interpret your site.

The following elements are managed for you:

- robots.txt, which tells search engines and bots which parts of your site they may or may not visit
- A sitemap, listing your pages so search engines can find and index them efficiently
- llms.txt, a file aimed at AI agents and language models, helping them understand your site
- Page titles and descriptions, shown in search results and used by bots and AI agents to understand what a page is about
- Structured data, which adds machine-readable information to your pages so search engines and AI agents can better interpret their content

Because these elements are generated and maintained by Easy2edit, you do not need to manually create or update robots.txt, sitemaps or structured data. The system keeps them in line with your site structure and content as it changes.

## FAQ

The FAQ module lets you publish your own frequently asked questions and answers on your website, available at the page /faq.

Key points about the FAQ module:

- You create and maintain the questions and answers yourself
- Questions and answers can be translated into all languages your site supports
- If a site was imported into Easy2edit, questions and answers that were found during the import are automatically placed into this module, so you do not have to recreate them manually
- The FAQ lives on its own page, /faq

To make sure visitors can find your FAQ page, add it to your site's menu.

1. Go to Admin > Pages
2. Locate or confirm the /faq page
3. Add this page to the menu so visitors can navigate to it directly

Once the FAQ page is in the menu, visitors can browse your questions and answers like any other page on your site.

## Statistics

The statistics section gives you an overview of how your website is performing, combining charts and figures in one place. It covers the whole site, including:

- Visitor numbers
- SEO performance
- Bot activity
- AI calls, such as requests coming from AI agents visiting your site

Statistics are organized clearly so you can see the overall picture as well as detailed information per module and plugin.

Each module and plugin that supports statistics gets its own tab or section within the statistics area. Modules and plugins write their own figures into this section, so you always see numbers that are relevant to the specific functionality you use.

An important detail to understand is that statistics depend on the module or plugin being active. If a particular plugin is switched off, nothing will be counted or shown for it in the statistics section. Turning a plugin back on resumes the counting, but data is not collected while it is disabled.

The statistics area uses widgets with charts to present the numbers visually, making it easy to spot trends in visitors, SEO performance, bot traffic and AI activity at a glance.

## Working with SEO, FAQ and statistics together

These three areas complement each other. Good SEO settings, including page titles, descriptions and structured data, make your pages easier to find and understand, both for traditional search engines and for AI agents. The FAQ module adds clear, structured content that can also be picked up by search engines and AI systems, strengthening your site's relevance for common questions. The statistics section then shows you the results, letting you see how visitors, bots and AI agents are actually interacting with your site.

A practical way to use these tools together:

1. Review your SEO settings to make sure page titles and descriptions are clear and accurate for your key pages
2. Build out your FAQ page with questions that reflect what your visitors commonly ask, and add it to your menu under Admin > Pages
3. Check the statistics section regularly to see how visitors, SEO and bot or AI activity are evolving over time
4. Use the per module and per plugin tabs in statistics to understand how specific features of your site are performing, keeping in mind that only active plugins will report figures

By keeping an eye on all three areas, you can continuously improve how your website is found, how well it answers visitor questions, and how it performs over time.
AI and AI credit

Easy2edit uses artificial intelligence (Claude, from Anthropic) throughout the system. The AI helps with translating texts, writing page content, importing websites, researching prices and more. Every time the AI is called, Easy2edit records who asked for it (a user, admin, superadmin or the system itself), from which part of the system the call came, which model was used, how many tokens went in and out, how long it took, whether it succeeded, and what it cost.

## The AI module

AI is a core module. It switches on automatically as soon as an AI link (an API key) is installed and enabled under Admin > API keys.

A link can be marked as a Superadmin link. When this is done, only superadmins can see or change it. This is used, for example, for the Easy2edit AI link and the Stripe link of the reseller. Unless an admin has set up his own AI and Stripe links (see below), AI calls made by users and admins always run on an Easy2edit link belonging to the superadmin.

## The Super admin AI dashboard

Super admin > AI gives superadmins a full view of AI use across the system, organised in tabs:

- Overview: key figures, cost over time per group, share of use per group, and the last calls made.
- Where: where AI is used most, what costs the most, which tasks and models are involved, and the busiest hours and weekdays.
- Users: heavy users and highest costs, with a table per user and a PDF button on each row.
- Costs: costs per month or week, broken down by group and by user.
- Credit: management of user and admin AI credit.
- Blocks: AI dashboard parts that can be placed on pages.
- Settings: pricing, margins and related configuration.

Filters are available for period, month (the current month plus the previous twelve) and group. The PDF button produces a summary, or, if 'Detailed' is chosen, a complete list of every call including tokens in and out, duration and cost.

## Costs, margins and pricing

Superadmins manage purchase prices per million tokens per model, organised in tabs for Claude, OpenAI and Gemini, showing the models currently active in the API. The 'Refresh models' button also looks up current prices directly from the AI provider. Purchase prices are shown in the purchase currency (for example USD).

Sale prices are shown in the selling currency (for example EUR), using an exchange rate that can be updated with a button that asks the AI for the current rate.

Three separate margins can be set, in percent, for tokens in and tokens out separately: for users, for admins, and for the reseller or superadmin.

A switch controls whether superadmin and system use is also charged to the customer. When this is on, that use is booked to a group named after the website, using the reseller margin. When it is off, that use is a cost to the reseller with no margin applied, and shown separately.

Prices, exchange rate and margins are stored with each individual call, so later changes only affect new calls, not past ones. Only superadmins can change these AI settings.

## AI credit

Users and admins normally need to buy AI credit before they can use AI; this requirement is switched on by default. Superadmins and the system itself never need credit.

Before every AI call, Easy2edit estimates the cost and checks it against the available credit. If there is not enough credit, nothing is sent, and a message explains how much is needed. After the call completes, the actual cost is deducted.

When a user's credit runs low, a pop-up appears with a slider. The minimum step is set to 25, 50 or 100, based on that user's use over the last 30 days, along with a suggested top-up amount.

Payment always goes through Stripe, using an Easy2edit link belonging to the superadmin. It never uses the Stripe account of the website's own shop. Credit is added once payment is confirmed as paid; this is checked when the customer returns from Stripe, and checked again when the AI screen is opened.

Superadmins set the top-up amounts and can manually add or deduct credit for any user, under Super admin > AI > Credit.

Every admin sees a welcome pop-up at first login, explaining how AI and AI credit work.

Each standard installation has an AI tab showing whether AI belongs to that installation, whether credit is required, and the smallest and largest top-up amounts allowed.

## AI use for admins

Admin > AI shows the AI use of users and admins, without purchase prices, margins or reseller costs. The Admin start page also shows a block called 'AI use', with the admin's own credit balance. There is a table per user and a PDF report per user, without purchase prices.

Viewing this requires the right 'View AI use of users', assigned through Roles.

An admin who has set up his own AI link (Anthropic) and his own Stripe link, neither marked as superadmin links, can switch on his own credit system for his users under Admin > AI > Credit for users. In that case, his users use his AI link, pay through his Stripe account, and the margin belongs to him. He sets his own credit rules, top-up amounts and margin, and can add credit per user.

## AI blocks

Parts of the AI dashboard, such as key figures, costs over time, use per group, where AI is used, heavy users, highest costs, models, and busy hours, can be switched on as system objects under Super admin > AI > Blocks and placed on a page in edit mode. These figures are only visible to superadmins.
Plugins, backups, licence and deployment

This chapter covers the parts of Easy2edit that keep your website running smoothly over time: plugins that extend what your site can do, backups that protect your work, the licence that determines what you pay, and the deployment setup that runs everything behind the scenes.

## Plugins

Plugins are signed packages that add extra functionality to your website. You manage them in Admin > Plugins.

A plugin can bring its own pages, modules, translations (available in 44 languages) and admin screens. In other words, installing a plugin can add new building blocks to your site and new menu items to your admin area, all at once.

To work with plugins:

1. Go to Admin > Plugins to see the plugins that are currently installed, stored in the /plugins folder.
2. Open the library (resource/plugins) to browse available plugins and install new ones.
3. Switch a plugin on or off as needed. Note that some features, such as statistics tracking, only work while the related plugin is switched on.
4. Use the update option to bring an installed plugin to its latest version.

Because plugins are signed packages, you can trust that what you install matches what the developer published.

## Backups

Backups protect the content and configuration of your website. You manage them in Admin > Backups.

Easy2edit creates backups on a daily, weekly or monthly basis. Each backup includes:

- Pages
- Menus
- Texts
- Images
- Theme
- Settings of modules and plugins

From the Backups screen you can restore a previous backup or download it for safekeeping elsewhere.

The standard installation basis is recorded in installations.json, which is part of the system itself. This file never contains secret keys, so it is safe to keep alongside your installation without exposing sensitive credentials.

## Licence

The licence determines the cost of running your Easy2edit website. You manage this in Admin > Licence, where you can see the cost and choose a payment method: Stripe or invoice.

The price of your licence follows directly from the modules and plugins you have switched on. The more functionality you use, the more your licence reflects that usage, so you only pay for what your site actually needs.

For super admins, there is an additional area under Super Admin > Prices, which includes:

- The price list per month, quarter and year
- Quotations that can be generated as PDF
- Marketing tiles for presenting pricing to customers
- Sales calculation tools

This gives super admins full control over how pricing is presented and calculated across installations.

## Deployment

Easy2edit is designed to run in Docker, with separate compose files for development and production environments. This separation lets you test changes safely before rolling them out to a live site.

A typical deployment setup includes:

- A reverse proxy and certificates to handle secure traffic
- The Easy2edit backend, which automatically runs any necessary database migrations when it starts

This means that when you update your installation, the backend takes care of bringing the database structure up to date without manual intervention.

Every installation displays its version clearly, in the format Easy2edit version 1.0.0 build X. This information comes from a single, central source: backend/BUILD. Having one authoritative source for the version number makes it easy to confirm exactly which build is running on any given installation, which is especially useful when troubleshooting or coordinating updates across multiple sites.

## How these pieces fit together

Plugins, backups, licensing and deployment are closely connected:

- Switching plugins on or off changes both your licence cost and what gets tracked in statistics.
- Backups capture not only your content but also the settings of whichever modules and plugins are active, so restoring a backup brings your site back to a consistent state.
- Deployment ensures that whatever combination of modules and plugins you run, the underlying infrastructure (database, proxy, certificates) stays in sync through automatic migrations.

Together, these tools give administrators a clear, practical way to manage the technical and financial side of an Easy2edit website, from day-to-day plugin management to long-term version tracking and cost control.
